\section[occupé]{occupé — busy}

\label{lesson:FR-C131-occupe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the French for brown, then the French for pretty.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: occupé}
\textbf{occupé} — \textquotedblleft{}busy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{occupé} is the past participle of the verb for \textquotedblleft{}to occupy\textquotedblright{}, a learned borrowing of Latin \emph{occupare}, \textquotedblleft{}to seize\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{ob} and \emph{capere}, \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

\section[ouvert]{ouvert — open}

\label{lesson:FR-C131-ouvert}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the French for busy, then the French for free.

\textbf{Ouvert} belongs to \textbf{ouvrir}, to open, which takes the endings of a verb in -er: \emph{j'ouvre}. Say \emph{j'ouvre}, then its opposite, \emph{je ferme}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: ouvert}
\textbf{ouvert} — \textquotedblleft{}open\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{ouvert} is the past participle of \emph{ouvrir}, \textquotedblleft{}to open\textquotedblright{}: opened. It goes back to Vulgar Latin \emph{*opertus}, from Latin \emph{apertus}, \textquotedblleft{}open\textquotedblright{}. (EtymDB 2.1)
\end{cousinweb}

\section[fermé]{fermé — closed}

\label{lesson:FR-C131-ferme}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the French for free, then the French for open.

\textbf{Fermé} is the closed form of \textbf{fermer}, to close. Say \emph{fermer}, then \emph{fermé}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: fermé}
\textbf{fermé} — \textquotedblleft{}closed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{fermé} is the past participle of \emph{fermer}, \textquotedblleft{}to close\textquotedblright{}: closed. The verb $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{firmare}, \textquotedblleft{}to make firm, to fasten\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[calme]{calme — calm, quiet}

\label{lesson:FR-C131-calme}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: calme}
\textbf{calme} — \textquotedblleft{}calm, quiet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{calme} $\leftarrow$ Italian \emph{calma} $\leftarrow$ Late Latin \emph{cauma}, \textquotedblleft{}the heat of midday\textquotedblright{}, from Greek \emph{kauma}, \textquotedblleft{}burning heat\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1) — borrowed: the still hour when the sun was hottest.
\end{cousinweb}
